triples.subject: ExitSlit
triples.context: The energy resolution of the synchrotron radiation beam is determined by the exit-slit width of the monochromator; the energy resolution is increased when the slit width is decreased.

triples.subject: SynchrotronRadiationBeam
triples.context: The energy resolution of the synchrotron radiation beam is determined by the exit-slit width of the monochromator; the energy resolution is increased when the slit width is decreased.

triples.subject: IonCloud
triples.context: However, the decrease in the monochromator slit width leads to the deterioration of the signal-to-noise ratio and the possible disappearance of the overlap between the ion cloud and photon beam.

triples.subject: HighlyChargedIon
triples.context: The HCIs are bred through electron-impact ionization in the EBIT trap region.

triples.subject: KShellElectron
triples.context: This electron energy is below the threshold for direct electron-impact excitation of K-shell electrons in He-like O6+(573.94 eV [46]), thereby suppressing direct excitation events, a source of background.

triples.subject: MShellElectron
triples.context: We set the electron beam energy to 1200 eV to efficiently breed Ne-like Fe16+ ions, the target of our measurement, which is approximately 2.5 times the ionization threshold energy of M-shell electrons in Na-like Fe15+, 489.256 eV [45], and lower than the ionization threshold energy of Ne-like Fe16+, 1262.7 eV [48].

triples.subject: HighlyChargedIon
triples.context: The electron beam at the probing energy of 250 eV cannot produce Ne-like Fe16+, resulting in a continuous depletion of Fe16+ due to radiative recombination and charge exchange processes [49], as well as the loss of HCIs from the trap [50]; thus, only the events from the first 200 ms in the probing phases are extracted (Fig. 4) for the analysis explained in the next section.
